title: Arsenal and the Scott chase: patience beats panic at Bournemouth
body:
Arsenal have reportedly contacted Bournemouth about midfielder Alex Scott [S1].

Sky Sports reported that Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool are all chasing the Bournemouth player [S2]. Elsewhere, Manchester United have added two defenders to their list of potential targets, and Aston Villa are weighing up a move for Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia [S1]. A crowded chase like this tells you more about newspaper competition than about any deal being close.

The form numbers add a wrinkle. Arsenal have won all five of their recent league matches, scoring 7 and conceding 1 [ST1]. Bournemouth have also been strong, winning four of their last five, though they have conceded 6 in that run [ST2]. A side on that kind of run has little reason to sell cheaply, and a club that is winning does not need to panic into a bad fee.

The side that wins this kind of race is usually the one that refuses to overpay for a rumour. Every move that has been linked so far is still just talk, and a club that bids too early tends to pay for it later.

The Touchline Take: judge the business when the window shuts, not before.
